chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Upon the one performing Tamattu' (with Umrah to Hajj) are three circuits around the House, and he prays two rak'ahs for each circuit, and two Sa'ys between As-Safa and Al-Marwah."

key_terms.أَطْوَافٍ: Circuits (plural of Tawaf), the ritual walking around the Kaaba.
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: Safa and Marwah, the two hills between which pilgrims walk.
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: The House, referring to the Kaaba in Mecca.
key_terms.الْعُمْرَةُ: Umrah, the minor pilgrimage performed before Hajj in this context.
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One performing Tamattu' Hajj, a type of pilgrimage where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately.
key_terms.سَعْيَانِ: Two rounds of Sa'y, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah.

ai.seo_question: What are the required rituals for Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the distinct ritual requirements for Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing the necessity of performing three separate Tawafs and two Sa'ys. This detailed prescription highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the Umrah and Hajj phases, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the specific acts of worship required for each stage of the combined pilgrimage.
